name: Music mastering
markdown:
# Music mastering

> From the author's earlier studio, cleaned for publication: private paths, ports and some lines were removed, so a step may read short and a screen it names may not exist here. Status in this studio: Untested.


## Why

`the author's research notes` measured this box's Music 3 songs: -13 to -14 LUFS with true peaks up to +0.3 dBTP (over the -1 dBTP target), the first second 8-19 dB under the file median (slow fade-ins), songs starting near -33 dB and ending near -48 dB so they do not loop cleanly. a streaming service's published figure is -14 LUFS integrated with 1 dB of true-peak headroom; **short-video publishes no figure**. This page is the fix, as an option, never a default.

## What it does (CPU only, numpy on `sound_dsp.py`, whose `master()` / `limit()` / `lufs()` / `true_peak_db()` / `loop_seam()` it calls and does not change)

Three steps in this order, each optional except the last:

1. **Fast start.** Find when the song's level first comes within 6 dB of its body level; cut at the strongest rise in level just before that (30 ms ahead of it, snapped to a zero crossing, 8 ms raised-cosine fade-in). It opens on its **first strong onset; that is not a verified downbeat.** An intro longer than 10 s or a quarter of the song is treated as intended and left alone; with no fade-in only dead air at the head is removed.
2. **Loop-ready end.** Looks in the last 40 s before the song's musical end for the point where the music that *follows* sounds like the music at the *start* (12-band energy match over 2 s, refined to the sample by cross-correlation), cuts there and overlays what followed onto the start with an equal-power 1 s crossfade, so the wrap is continuous. If nothing matches (mean difference over 4.5 dB), the song is only trimmed at its musical end and **the card says it will not loop seamlessly**. The result is re-checked with `sound_dsp.loop_seam()` and both seam checks are on the card.
3. **Loudness.** `sound_dsp.master()`: gain to the preset, then a look-ahead true-peak limiter. A peaky song that needs more than 6 dB of limiting stops short of the target and says so (the peak ceiling wins over the loudness target). The limiter ceiling is -1.2 dBTP (0.2 dB under the stated -1); the **written file is then re-measured with two estimators** (ours and ffmpeg `loudnorm`) and trimmed and rewritten if either reads over -1 dBTP.

| Preset | Target | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `streaming` | -14 LUFS, true peak at or under -1 dBTP | a streaming service's published reference |

Output: 24-bit FLAC at the song's own sample rate (32-96 kHz kept, else 44.1 kHz), metadata-free, mono stays mono. Songs longer than 15 minutes are refused.

**Honest limits.** Loudness targets are conventions. DSP changes the level, the first and last seconds and the peaks; it **cannot fix a bad mix, a flat arrangement or a bad vocal**, and it cannot repair clipping that is already in the file. Fast start and loop-ready change the song's length and its arrangement on purpose.

## Where it is

| Place | How | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| **Music tab, all five engines** (`music:music3`, `ace_turbo`, `yue2`, `sa3`, `ace_base`, and `df:minimax_music:music`) | three settings chips: `master` (off / streaming / loud), `master_start` (as rendered / fast start), `master_tail` (as rendered / loop-ready). Start and end chips act only when Master is not off | result artifact 0 = the **raw take, untouched**; artifact 1 = the mastered file (`mastered_from: 0`, `master` block). The card shows raw against mastered: LUFS, true peak, first-second level (and against the body), start level (first 0.25 s), end level (last 0.5 s), length, clean-loop yes/no, each step in words. Artifact 1 is an ordinary audio artifact, so the output guard, the song pickers and the Post steps work on it. A failure to master never loses the render: the raw take is kept and carries `master_error`. The mastered file is `<raw>_master-<preset>[-fast][-loop].flac` beside the raw one and a rerun reuses it |
| **Song recreate** (single and batch) | form option "Master after render" in the target settings; `master` in `POST /api/studio/songrecreate/start` and `/batch/start` | the song job carries the chips; the run's result points at the mastered file (`result.index` 1, `raw_url`, `master`) |
| **Music video maker** | same option on a generated song (`song.master`); a library, uploaded or studio-result song is used as it is | the song stage uses the mastered file; the SHORT quality check adds the trimmed seconds back so a loop-ready cut does not trigger a new seed |
| **Song library** | "Master this song" on every row (Details > Check this song) | a `song:master` CPU job writes a **new library song** titled "<title> (mastered, ...)", `provenance: "mastered from <id>"`, `mastered_from` block (options, before, after, steps, verified numbers), the source's analysis moved by the cut and marked derived, loudness updated; the source gets a `used_in` entry (`kind: master`). Never overwrites; the same source + options is the same copy |
| **Check a song** | same Details panel, and `POST /api/studio/mastering/measure` for a library song or a studio result | the numbers above, plain advice (over -1 dBTP, quiet intro, no clean loop point, lead silence, clipping, mono), the suggested options, and the Sound maker checklist lines (`sound_maker_fit.score`, class hook, read-only) |
| **Measure all** | "Measure all (report)" under the library list, the earlier studio's mastering_report module | see below |

## Routes (all under `/api/studio/mastering/`, handler `scripts/chatbox/server.py::_mastering_route`)

`GET /config` (presets, chips, notes) · `GET /report` (last measure-all report and run status) · `POST /measure {song_id}` or `{session_id, result:{job_id,index}}` (runs in the request, a few seconds for a 3-minute song) · `POST /song {session_id, song_id, preset, fast_start?, loop_ready?}` (queues the `song:master` job; Retry works) · `POST /measure-all {limit?}` (starts the detached niced report; 409 while one is alive).

## Measure all (read-only, CPU, niced, resumable)

The earlier studio's mastering_report module (options: library, output folder, limit) opens each song's `audio.flac` once and measures it. It never changes a song, a `meta.json` or the library folder. `report.json` is rewritten after every song, so killing it and running it again continues; a song whose file size and mtime match its saved entry is skipped. Output (outside the library): `a local folder` (`report.json`, `report.md`, `status.json`, `run.log`; `COMFY_MASTERING_STATE_DIR` overrides).

**Run 2026-10-17 on the real library (132 songs, all imported from long-form video, 6.1 hours, about 9 minutes niced):** 104 would clip (true peak over -1 dBTP; 87 of them over 0), 80 have the first second 6+ dB under the body, 122 have no clean loop point, 20 are quiet (under -16.5 LUFS), 93 are louder than -12.5 LUFS (median -9.9 LUFS, highest true peak +2.3 dBTP). **These are commercial masters from the author's imports, not Music 3 renders**, so they say little about the Music 3 findings above: mastering such a song to -14 LUFS would turn it *down*, and a quiet intro in a commercial song is usually intended. Fast start would cut 92 of them, median 0.35 s (so mostly dead air), longest 9.9 s. The numbers are the measure-all definitions, not a verdict on any song.

## Tests that ran (not just wired)

`tests/studio/test_mastering_dsp.py` (16): measure; fast start on a beat, left alone with no fade-in or a long intro, dead air; loop-ready (seam before fails, after passes, whole beats) and the no-match case; loudness within +-0.5 LU of -14 and -12; true peak at or under -1 dBTP for a +0.3 dBTP song and for a signal whose reconstructed wave overshoots its samples; a peaky song that cannot reach -12 says so; silence refused; mono stays mono. `tests/studio/test_mastering.py` (21, real ffmpeg): the options, the chips on every music engine, the written file measured again by ffmpeg `loudnorm` (+-0.5 LU, true peak at or under -1 dBTP), raw bytes unchanged, mastered artifact linked and reused, failure keeps the raw take, library copy with provenance and no overwrite and no half-song on failure, the `song:master` job and its `used_in`, check advice. `tests/studio/test_mastering_report.py` (5): read-only (hash of the whole library before and after), resumable, niced, one run at a time. `tests/chatbox/test_mastering_routes.py` (8), the three maker tests in `test_songrecreate.py`, `test_songrecreate_batch.py`, `test_musicvideo.py`, and `tests/chatbox/js/mastering_helpers.test.mjs` (8).

## For the Post steps (not wired: `post.py` and `PostPanel.js` belong to another change)

Nothing is needed for a mastered song to work in the Post steps: it is an ordinary audio artifact (index 1 of the music job). A later "Master" step on a post card could call `mastering.master_file(src, dest, {"preset": ..., "fast_start": ..., "loop_ready": ...})` directly, or `POST /api/studio/mastering/song` for a library song; the platform loudness table in `post.PLATFORM` could map its `lufs` to a preset. Not done here.

## Not done / limits

- Nobody has listened to a mastered file. Next step: master three real Music 3 songs from the Music tab and compare (`readiness.json` family `music.mastering`, proof level recipe).
- Fast start finds a strong onset, not a downbeat; a song with a deliberate slow build is left alone only up to 10 s.
- Loop-ready works on repeating music; a through-composed song gets only a trim and a "will not loop seamlessly" note.
- The true-peak estimators agree to about 0.1 dB on limited music; the guard is two estimators plus a 0.2 dB margin, not a proof for every possible file.
- A mastered copy's analysis (beats, sections) is the source's moved by the cut, marked derived, not re-analysed.
- `POST /measure` runs inside the request; a 15-minute song takes tens of seconds.
